name: Glean
style: hybrid: (a) crawl+index into vendor tenant is the default; (b) live and hybrid access exist per connector; MCP tools fetch live or act but do not make content searchable
permissions: Connectors retrieve each source's permissions map and mirror it into the index; some connectors (SharePoint, GitHub Server) also check access at query time; live connectors may need end-user auth
freshness: Webhooks where the source supports them, else incremental crawls; SharePoint falls back to ~24h permission updates without webhook scope; custom Interact connectors run scheduled crawls with no real-time permission sync
connectors: '275+ out-of-the-box connectors' per https://www.glean.com/connectors (vendor marketing)
storage: Content and permissions stored in an isolated Glean tenant
pricing: not public; third-party estimates only (Vendr median contract $98,890/yr, $30-48/seat/mo reported) via https://www.gosearch.ai/blog/glean-pricing-explained
notes: Indexing SDK handles identity crawl first, groups must carry memberships (https://developers.glean.com/libraries/indexing-sdk/concepts/architecture). Webhook setup for SharePoint needs Files.ReadWrite.All (search snippet at https://docs.glean.com/connectors/native/sharepoint/set-up-indexing-connector).

name: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors (Graph connectors, semantic index)
style: hybrid: synced connectors ingest and semantically index into Microsoft Graph; federated connectors fetch at query time over MCP with no data movement
permissions: Synced: Entra ID app registration; deployed connectors are tenant-wide unless external item security is restricted. Federated: MCP auth (OAuth 2.0 or service-specific)
freshness: Synced: depends on connector crawl/ingest code (not specified on page). Federated: real-time API calls
connectors: 'More than 100 connectors' in the gallery per Microsoft Learn
storage: Synced content stored in Microsoft Graph; federated content not stored; citations point to MCP-returned content
pricing: not public for connectors; Copilot add-on about $30/user/mo per third-party blogs (https://www.epcgroup.net/microsoft-365-copilot-licensing-cost-enterprise-2026)
notes: Federated connectors do not support semantic indexing; Microsoft says semantic indexing helps topic queries but not counts or multi-parameter queries. Page dated 2026-09-30.

name: Gemini Enterprise (formerly Agentspace)
style: hybrid: ingested connectors copy into per-entity data stores; federated connectors query the source API directly and store nothing; where both exist the admin chooses
permissions: Identity syncs capture users tied to ACL groups; access control set per data source; federated queries run against the source API
freshness: Entity full sync every 3h to 7d; identity sync every 30min to 7d; incremental every 3h by default (no deletions, no identity data)
connectors: Docs navigation lists roughly 130 third-party connectors (fetch summary count, not a vendor-stated figure)
storage: Ingested data in selected region (global/US/EU) with Google-managed or CMEK keys; federated stores nothing
pricing: not public in sources fetched; third-party blogs report about $21 Business, $30 Standard, $50-60 Plus per user per month (https://www.gosearch.ai/faqs/gemini-enterprise-pricing/)
notes: Docs warn federated query strings may carry parts of conversation and go to all enabled backends. Release note 2026-08-31: federated data stores supported in FedRAMP High Assured Workloads (search snippet https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/release-notes).

name: Atlassian Rovo (Teamwork Graph connectors)
style: hybrid: synced connectors (admin-set, best quality), direct connectors (live via provider search APIs, not stored or indexed), Smart Link connectors (per-user)
permissions: Restricted third-party content visible only to users with access in the source; Smart Link results use each user's own permissions
freshness: Rovo keeps a sync with the app as content is created or removed; no timing published (https://support.atlassian.com/organization-administration/docs/how-connector-permissions-are-kept-in-sync/)
connectors: not public as a single count in pages retrieved
storage: Synced content in Atlassian Teamwork Graph; direct connectors not stored
pricing: Included in paid Cloud plans per an Atlassian Community reply; credit allowances per third-party; not verified on Atlassian price page
notes: Most connectors connectable once per Rovo site. Rovo Studio and some connectors reportedly Premium/Enterprise only (community thread).

name: Notion AI Enterprise Search + Connectors
style: not public: help center does not say whether connected content is indexed or queried live
permissions: not public on the Enterprise Search page
freshness: not public
connectors: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, Jira named; no total count found
pricing: Business and Enterprise plans only; price not captured
notes: Search defaults to workspace, connected apps and the web; user can pick GPT, Claude or Gemini models.

name: Slack Real-time Search API + MCP server
style: (b) live federated query: RTS API retrieves Slack data without bulk download or third-party storage; MCP server exposes tools to AI clients
permissions: User OAuth tokens; granular scopes search:read.public (required), search:read.private/.im/.mpim need user consent; results limited to what the user can see
freshness: Live at query time (no index); Events API available for push (30,000 deliveries/workspace/app/hour)
connectors: MCP partner clients named include Claude.ai, Claude Code, Perplexity, Cursor
storage: Slack keeps the data; API Terms bar third parties from keeping persistent copies, archives or indexes of other orgs' RTS/Data Access API data
notes: Only directory-published or internal apps may use MCP (https://docs.slack.dev/ai/slack-mcp-server/). MCP rate limits mirror Web API tiers (Tier 2 to Tier 4). Since 2025-05-29 unlisted commercial apps get 1 req/min and 15 objects on conversations.history/replies (https://docs.slack.dev/changelog/2025/05/29/rate-limit-changes-for-non-marketplace-apps). API ToS: https://slack.com/terms-of-service/api

name: ChatGPT company knowledge / apps with sync
style: hybrid: admin-managed sync builds an index of selected content; apps also connect for live access
permissions: Synced content respects source permissions after initial indexing per help pages; admins choose scope; older pages say Drive access follows non-synced access
freshness: not public in snippets
connectors: Connectors renamed apps in Dec 2025; app directory migrated to plugin directory (July 9, 2026 update per snippet); count not public
storage: Synced index stored by OpenAI (2025 beta reporting: encrypted copy) ; no generalized model training on Business/Enterprise/Edu workspace data by default
pricing: apps with sync only on select paid plans; prices not captured
notes: Official page returned 403 to fetch; relying on search snippets, so details may be stale. Individual user sync reportedly discontinued in favour of admin-managed sync.

name: Claude connectors / remote MCP / enterprise search
style: (b) live federated query via MCP; no vendor-side index described
permissions: Claude inherits each user's permissions in the connected service; per-user authentication; owners can set tool permissions Always allow / Needs approval / Blocked; enterprise-managed auth (beta)
freshness: Live at call time
connectors: count not public; Microsoft 365, Slack, Google Drive etc. named in search snippets
storage: No index described; on Team and Enterprise, connectors work only in private projects and chats with synced content cannot be shared
pricing: Connectors on Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise (docs); Enterprise Search 'Ask Your Org' project is described only by third-party blogs
notes: Custom remote MCP servers must be internet-reachable from Anthropic cloud, unless IP allowlisting is used. Third-party services process data under their own terms.

name: Dust
style: (a) ingest into Dust, plus MCP tools for live actions
permissions: Data placed in Company Data or per-space; admin selects channels, folders, pages; space membership controls access (not mirrored per-document from source in pages seen)
freshness: A few minutes for updates to appear per docs snippet
connectors: Docs name Confluence, Google Drive, GitHub, Notion, Slack, Snowflake, Zendesk, Intercom, SharePoint
notes: Slack excludes group DMs, external files; GitHub syncs issues, PRs, discussions but not code; Drive skips large extracted text (limits inconsistent across pages).

name: Sana (now Workday)
style: (a) sync-based real-time ingestion; private integrations tied to a user's account permissions
permissions: Integrated systems can mirror source permissions; shared integrations may show content to users who lack source access unless admin narrows audience
freshness: Described as real-time sync
connectors: count not public; custom MCP connectors supported (https://doc.workday.com/admin-guide/en-us/workday-ai/sana-for-workday/concept--sana-workspace.html)
notes: Free tier limited to Drive, SharePoint, calendars; Enterprise has wider set.

name: Guru
style: (a) sync sources into Guru, with optional inherited permissions
permissions: Optional inherited permissions mirror source access; otherwise assigned to Guru Groups; SCIM supported
freshness: not public
connectors: count not public; Slack, Teams, Google Workspace, Salesforce named by Gartner listing
notes: Slack source needs the Guru bot invited to each channel. Page and Collection access does not inherit from parent.

name: Moveworks Enterprise Search
style: hybrid by connector: indexed (mirror content and permissions) or live API (user-impersonated search at query time, nothing stored)
permissions: Permissions mirrored into a permissions store, pre- and post-retrieval filtering; live calls use the user's OAuth token
freshness: Max Capacity connectors advertise improved freshness; live connectors are real time
connectors: Classic: 35+ content systems, up to 100K docs per connector; Max Capacity: nine systems, up to 100M docs each (search snippet)
storage: Indexed connectors store in Moveworks; live (SharePoint/OneDrive, Slack, Outlook on Max Capacity) store nothing
notes: Doc lists ServiceNow, Confluence, SharePoint, Drive, Zendesk as indexed; Outlook, Jira, Box, Slack as live.

name: Perplexity Enterprise connectors
style: not public: index vs live not documented in sources retrieved
permissions: not public
freshness: not public
connectors: Help center lists Google Drive, Confluence, Slack, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams
pricing: Enterprise Pro tier gate per 2025 report; price not captured
notes: Conflicting third-party report that internal search covered only uploaded files; treat as unresolved.

name: Writer connectors
style: (b) live via MCP gateway; OpenAPI or MCP custom connectors
permissions: Admin-managed in AI Studio; read/write capability split per tool; per-tool-operation controls
freshness: Live, plus event triggers (new Salesforce record, Slack message)
connectors: count not public; Drive, Salesforce, Jira, Slack named
notes: Hebbia: no source found in this research; not covered.

name: Coveo Unified Index
style: (a) crawl+index into a unified index
permissions: Connectors pull permissions from source and save them as item metadata; source-level permission fallback gives all-or-none access
freshness: not public in snippets
connectors: not public
notes: Third-party profile claims a Feb 2026 hosted MCP server; unconfirmed on Coveo's own pages.

name: Elastic search connectors
style: (a) crawl+index into your own Elasticsearch
permissions: Document-level security for selected connectors (Confluence, Dropbox, Jira, GitHub, Gmail, Drive, OneDrive, Salesforce, SharePoint Online, ServiceNow and others); enforced via API keys with DLS
freshness: Sync jobs (schedule configurable); not detailed in snippets
connectors: DLS list above; total count not captured
storage: Self-managed or Elastic Cloud index; access to index must be at least as restrictive as source
notes: Elastic warns the synced index itself is the weak point.

name: Salesforce Data 360 (Data Cloud) zero-copy + Agentforce
style: (c) zero-copy: query federation and file federation over Iceberg (Snowflake, Databricks, AWS Lake Formation); data sharing
permissions: Only Databricks credential vending detailed (temporary access via Unity Catalog); broader model not described in the page
freshness: Live read of the lake; no cache described
connectors: Warehouses/lakes only (Snowflake, Databricks, Lake Formation, any Iceberg REST catalog), not SaaS apps
pricing: A Salesforce evaluation guide cites 70 credits per million records for federation vs 2,000 for batch ingestion; treat as unverified (https://www.salesforce.com/en-us/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/documents/resources/self-service-evaluation-guide.pdf)
notes: File Federation was Beta in the fetched article (date unknown). Zero-copy works for structured warehouse data, not for Slack or Notion.

name: Databricks Lakehouse Federation (query federation)
style: (c) zero-copy: queries pushed down to the foreign database over JDBC; read-only
permissions: Unity Catalog securables on foreign catalogs; connection holds credentials
freshness: Live
connectors: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Teradata, Oracle, Redshift, Salesforce Data 360, Snowflake, SQL Server, Synapse, BigQuery, Databricks
notes: Docs recommend Lakeflow Connect for high volume and low latency; Spark Data Source API where unsupported or writes needed.

name: Supermemory Company Brain
style: Slack agent on a Cloudflare Worker with one Durable Object per org; stores derived memory, not pointers; hybrid search, 40 results per container, threshold 0.3; hosted product discontinued and open-sourced (changelog dated 2026-07-24)
permissions: Container-level lists from a membership table, not per document: shared memory for public channels, one container per private channel, one per person for DMs; no live recheck described
freshness: Memory written as people talk; no change feed or sweep described
connectors: Granola, PostHog, Linear, GitHub, Sentry, Gmail, Notion, Plain named
storage: Postgres through Hyperdrive plus Supermemory memory containers; hybrid search, 40 results per container, threshold 0.3
notes: Marketed as 'company brain'. Read from the open-source repo and changelog: hosted product discontinued and open-sourced (changelog dated 2026-07-24); about 1.1k stars, 150 forks. Slack writes pause for Approve or Deny and only the asker can decide. Org-shared tool connections are read-only. A teammate can lend a personal tool connection for one request (10-minute grant, 15-minute expiry); Gmail is personal-only and cannot be lent. No leak test or erasure path described.
